html:
The Patwin are the southern branch of the Wintun peoples of Northern California, living on the west side of the lower Sacramento Valley and in the nearby hills of the Coast Range. Wintun speakers have lived in California since about 500 CE.

Patwin villages stood along the Sacramento River and its creeks. They lived on acorns, salmon and other fish, game, waterbirds, seeds and tule reeds, and traded with neighbours such as the Pomo and Miwok. They took part in the Kuksu religion, with dances by costumed dancers in large earth covered roundhouses.

In the early 1800s some Patwin were drawn into the Spanish missions. A malaria epidemic in 1833 devastated the Sacramento Valley, and the Gold Rush after 1848 brought settlers and violence. Today Patwin people belong to three federally recognised tribes, among them the Yocha Dehe Wintun Nation. Their relatives to the north include the Northern Wintu.
